clue.text: A maiden leaves surprise new arrival, a small primate

indicators.note: the letters for 'A maiden' depart from the word for surprise, so they are taken away

parts.note: to ambush someone is to surprise them
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a baby is a newly arrived child

explanation.surface: A young woman runs off, startled by a newborn that turns out to be a tiny primate.
explanation.definitionFit: The galago of Africa is a small nocturnal primate with big eyes, commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Garment featuring in ripping drama?

parts.note: a 'ripper' is a racy historical romance, whose heroine's tight top gets torn

explanation.surface: A costume features in an exciting play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripping' looks like 'excellent' but alludes to the 'bodice-ripper' genre of steamy period romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting woman's upper garment, torn in the clichéd scenes of racy period novels.

clue.text: Reddish-brown parrots heading north across India

indicators.note: the reversed word lies across, around, the letter for India
in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: to parrot is to ape, imitate
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Reddish-brown parrots fly north over India.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm brown pigment from cuttlefish ink, the tone of old photographs.

clue.text: Where to wash tiger's head in animal centre

parts.note: a bat is an animal

indicators.note: the tiger's first letter goes inside the animal-and-centre pair

parts.note: a hub is a centre

indicators.note: only the first letter of 'tiger's' is taken

explanation.surface: A zookeeper wonders where to wash a tiger's head in the animal centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub filled with water for bathing in, a place to get clean.

clue.text: Chocolate cake indicates what good deeds can earn you?

definitions.text: what good deeds can earn you?

parts.note: a brownie is a small square chocolate cake
points means shows or indicates

explanation.surface: A chocolate cake reward suggests what good behaviour earns.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional credit earned by doing favours to gain approval, idiomatically.

clue.text: A criminal admits beginning to sell out

indicators.note: the crooked word lets the opening letter of 'sell' come inside it

parts.note: bent is slang for corrupt or criminal

indicators.note: only the first letter of 'sell' is taken

explanation.surface: A crook confesses to starting to sell out his associates.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not present is away, not in: a common synonym pairing.

clue.text: Noble fellow from a Bronte novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of 'a Bronte' are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman out of a Brontë novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary titled rank below a baron, styled Sir: a member of the lesser nobility.

clue.text: Flower I planted in weedless ground

indicators.note: the letter I is set in, as a plant in the soil
ground means crushed, so the letters of 'weedless' are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener sets a flower in a bed free of weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil but is the anagram signal, giving EDELWESS for the I to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A white alpine plant of Europe, famous from The Sound of Music.

clue.text: Study of the Divine Comedy finally follows the old official account

indicators.note: the final letter of 'Comedy' comes after the other parts

parts.note: a log is an official record, account

indicators.note: only the last letter of 'Comedy' is used

explanation.surface: Dante's Divine Comedy is studied after an old official account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine Comedy' looks like one title, but the definition stops at Divine.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic discipline concerned with God and religious belief.

clue.text: Swim with hot skimpy garment: Kate has one!

parts.note: a dip is a short swim
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a thong is very skimpy underwear or swimwear

explanation.surface: A swimmer in a revealing thong prompts the remark that Kate owns one too.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: the vowel in the name Kate glides from one sound to another, so Kate 'has one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'ay' vowel in Kate is a gliding double vowel sound, the textbook example of this phonetic term.

clue.text: Microbe spread a nameless disease

parts.note: a germ is a microbe

indicators.note: the letters of 'nameless' are spread about, rearranged

explanation.surface: A microbe has spread an unidentified disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, a mild viral infection causing a rash, is a disease.

clue.text: Old magistrate constantly returning to drink last of wine

indicators.note: the reversed word swallows the final letter of 'wine', as a drinker takes it in
the word for constantly is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always, constantly

indicators.note: only the final letter of 'wine' is used

explanation.surface: An old magistrate keeps going back for the dregs of the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval England this officer was a local magistrate or steward of a manor or shire.

clue.text: Cow caught fly

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to fly is to hurry, hasten

explanation.surface: A cow manages to snap up a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to subdue or intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to subdue or discipline them into submission, much as punishment humbles.

clue.text: Frenchman backing legislation for redevelopment

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: the word for legislation is put in reverse order

parts.note: law is legislation

explanation.surface: A Frenchman supports a new law to allow redevelopment.
explanation.definitionFit: Regeneration of a run-down area, rebuilding it afresh, is a synonym for redevelopment.

clue.text: Gibraltar sent new threat of military action

indicators.note: the letters of 'Gibraltar sent' are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Gibraltar has sent a fresh threat of military action, a nod to its disputed sovereignty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes brandishing swords noisily: a show of aggression threatening armed force.

clue.text: Warm garment initially sheltering Uriah's family?

indicators.note: only the first letter of 'sheltering' is used

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield; his relations are Heep's kin

explanation.surface: A warm coat shelters the family of Uriah Heep.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat or jacket made of a fleece-covered hide keeps you warm.

clue.text: Son rejected flat

parts.note: quashed means rejected, overturned

explanation.surface: A son is turned down for a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home but is the adjective: pressed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crushed and pressed down becomes flattened, so the adjective works.

clue.text: Interview a revolutionary on the radio???

parts.note: to interview someone is to question them

indicators.note: words heard on the radio are spoken, so the revolutionary's name stands for a word sounding the same

parts.note: Karl Marx, the revolutionary thinker

explanation.surface: A radio journalist plans to interview a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The three printed symbols at the end are themselves the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbols ??? are three instances of the punctuation used to end an enquiry.

clue.text: Put radical in chains for inflammatory speeches

indicators.note: the short word for radical goes in the word for chains

parts.note: ties are bonds, chains

explanation.surface: A radical is put in chains for delivering inflammatory speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry outbursts or rants are heated, rabble-rousing addresses.

clue.text: University official holding a dangerous part of plant

indicators.note: the official's title holds the letter A inside it

parts.note: a rector is the head of some universities

explanation.surface: A university official keeps hold of a dangerous part of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks botanical but means an industrial installation, here a nuclear power station.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of a nuclear power station is a hazardous component of the facility.

clue.text: Manage to attend party

parts.note: to make a meeting is to attend it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone manages to go to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to get by or cope with what is available.

clue.text: Hoping not to finish pain medication

indicators.note: the word for hoping loses its final letter, so it does not finish

parts.note: aspiring means hoping or aiming

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to avoid taking the full course of their pain medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A common analgesic tablet, acetylsalicylic acid, taken to relieve pain.

clue.text: State where scientists may work with a master's degree

parts.note: a lab, a laboratory, is where scientists work
MA, Master of Arts, is a master's degree

explanation.surface: A scientist with a master's degree wonders which US state to work in.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states, in the Deep South, capital Montgomery.

clue.text: Wrong a lady

parts.note: Miss is the title of a young lady

explanation.surface: A woman is in error.
explanation.definitionFit: When things go wrong they go awry: a synonym for faulty or out of order.

clue.text: Marched president into empty helipad

indicators.note: the president's nickname goes inside the outer letters
helipad is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A president marches into a deserted helipad.
explanation.definitionFit: To have walked a long way purposefully, as on a trek, is close to having marched.

clue.text: So started a blaze, cutting first bit of fresh game

parts.note: lit as in started a fire

indicators.note: the opening letter of 'fresh' is cut out of the word for blaze

parts.note: a blaze is a fire

indicators.note: only the first letter of 'fresh' is used

explanation.surface: Someone started a blaze, and fresh fuel catches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started a blaze' reads as one action, but the blaze is a separate piece, and 'cutting' removes the opening of 'fresh' from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game played alone, also called patience, is a game for one.

clue.text: Fly around in returning from Scandinavia

indicators.note: the word for fly goes around the reversed 'in'

parts.note: to fly is to dash, rush

indicators.note: the word 'in' is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A traveller flies around on the return trip from Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian country, so its people and things are Scandinavian.

clue.text: Energy beginning to soar, keep going without finishing coffee

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: only the first letter of 'soar' is used
the phrase for keep going loses its last letter

parts.note: to press on is to keep going

explanation.surface: An energy boost from coffee helps you soar and press on without finishing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong black coffee brewed by forcing steam through ground beans.
